rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uproots Arab polytheism and soothsaying by explaining the realities of angels and jinn, which had supplied their foundations.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān by explaining the reality behind angels and the jinn has uprooted both these bases.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming section recounts the Day of Judgement to expose the fate of false deities and those who worshipped them instead of God.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to bring to the fore the fate of the deities as well as of those who are worshipping these deities while leaving aside God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage depicts idol leaders and their followers cursing one another on Judgement Day.
rows.anchor: The way the leaders of the Idolaters and their followers will mutually curse one another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also depicts believers holding to monotheism and the Hereafter despite opposition.
rows.anchor: the believers adhered to the beliefs of monotheism and the Hereafter in spite of all the opposition

none: English translation of the Qur’anic passage only.
English translation of the Qur’anic passage only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because deniers deem resurrection improbable, the Prophet is told to compare creating humans with creating the heavens, earth, seas, mountains, sun, and moon; God can recreate humans as readily as he first created them.
rows.anchor: So how can the God Who is able to create these things out of nothingness not be able to create a trivial thing as a human being again.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means sticky or clinging clay; God made these things with clay and needed no specially obtained raw material.
rows.anchor: What is implied is that the Almighty created all these things with clinging clay; no particular raw material was needed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clay is abundant and at God’s disposal, so the one who created humans initially can recreate them whenever he wills.
rows.anchor: The clay with which they were made is at the disposal of the Almighty in large quantities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading takes min as comparing humans with other created beings: humans are from clay, angels from light, and jinn from fire, so their recreation is no challenge.
rows.anchor: We created these people from clay and the angels and the jinn from light and fire respectively

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience’s mockery questions how a sensible and sagacious person could make the Prophet’s claim about resurrection.
rows.anchor: sensible and sagacious person make such a claim.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his audience are mentally as far apart as east and west; he fails to gauge the distance, so their attitude worries him.
rows.anchor: he and his addressees are as far apart from one another as the East and the West

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This mental gulf makes reminders and warnings useless: advice is wasted and no reasoning affects them.
rows.anchor: all his reminders and warnings are useless for them; whatever advice they are sounded goes waste; no reasoning has any effect on them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the greatest miracle cannot persuade them: they taunt the Prophet for demanding the Hereafter, then mock signs as plain magic.
rows.anchor: The verse says that the greatest of miracles cannot convince such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ridicule resurrection after death and the raising of their forefathers as irrational, and deem those who warn them mad.
rows.anchor: they think that all these things are far away from sense and reason. Hence, they think that those who threaten them of these things are mad.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since their question was jesting, the answer is stern: they will indeed be raised and humiliated.
rows.anchor: They are told that indeed they shall be raised to life again and at that time they will be disgraced and humiliated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Re-creation needs no special effort: one shout will suddenly raise them from their graves, as also described in 79:13–14.
rows.anchor: This will happen through a mere shout. With the sounding of this scream they will suddenly rise from their graves and start to look around.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single-shout scene conveys horror and dread without requiring further words.
rows.anchor: The horror and dread found in this style does not need any words for its expression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the denied Hereafter arrives, the people curse themselves and acknowledge that it has come.
rows.anchor: they will curse themselves and say that what they had been denying has arrived.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels answer that this is precisely the Judgement Day the people had denied.
rows.anchor: This is the reply they will receive from the angels: Yes this is the very day you had been denying.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wronged themselves are polytheists, especially their leaders, because polytheism is the greatest injustice.
rows.anchor: because polytheism is the greatest injustice. Contextual indication shows that the allusion is to the leaders among the polytheists.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwāj here means companions, followers, and associates.
rows.anchor: The word اجَوْزَأُ here is used for companions, followers and associates.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of worship include jinn deities associated with God, along with idols and stones.
rows.anchor: refers to the jinn deities they associated with God and the idols and stones they worshipped.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will direct the angels to gather the polytheists, their companions, and their objects of worship, then lead them to Hell.
rows.anchor: the Almighty will direct the angels to gather all of them and lead them to Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene humiliates the condemned by halting them for questioning about their inability to help one another.
rows.anchor: Stop them for a while so that a question can be posed to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Former leaders and followers no longer help each other, nor do worshippers and deities benefit or care for one another; all are absorbed in themselves.
rows.anchor: neither are the leaders helping their followers nor are the followers being of help to their leaders

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts the previous world’s mutual championing with universal selfishness at the moment when selflessness is needed.
rows.anchor: now is the time for selflessness but everyone has become selfish.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istislām means consigning oneself or obeying; the once arrogant now submit and have laid down their arms.
rows.anchor: today these people have become very obedient and submissive; till yesterday they were supercilious and arrogant; today they have laid down their arms.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasā’ul means mutual questioning; the following verses describe the altercation between leaders and followers.
rows.anchor: connotes “mutual questioning” and in the succeeding verses details are forthcoming about the altercation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context indicates that the masses speak first, blaming their leaders, who immediately answer in the second verse.
rows.anchor: first verse is uttered by the masses and second by the leaders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masses accuse their leaders of surrounding them from all sides and blocking them from hearing the Prophet; they say they would have believed otherwise.
rows.anchor: the right and the left so that we were not able to hear out the Prophet of God; if

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders interrupt to reject the accusation as baseless and say the masses would never have believed.
rows.anchor: this blame of theirs is totally baseless; they would never have embraced faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes struggled with the phrase about coming from the right because they missed a Qur’anic conversational device: an addressee interrupts to clear himself of blame.
rows.anchor: an addressee interrupts him and tries
